question.prompt:
In an arcade game, the “monster” is the shaded sector of a circle of radius \(1\) cm, as shown in the figure. The missing piece (the mouth) has central angle \(60^\circ.\) What is the perimeter of the monster in cm?

[Figure 1](figures/1985_AMC_12_Q02_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The perimeter includes both the curved boundary and the two straight edges of the mouth. Each straight edge is a radius, so together they have length \(2\) cm.

The remaining arc has central angle \(360^\circ-60^\circ=300^\circ\), so it is \(300/360=5/6\) of the full circumference. Since the radius is \(1\) cm, its length is
\[
\frac56(2\pi\cdot1)=\frac{5\pi}{3}\text{ cm}.
\]
Adding the two radii gives the perimeter
\[
\boxed{\frac{5\pi}{3}+2\text{ cm}},
\]
which is choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
solutions.title: Add the remaining arc and the mouth edges
